analysis.investment_thesis: Magic Formula fails here: earnings yield of ~6.7% (EBIT 6 Cr / EV ~90 Cr) is below my 12% threshold, even though the stated ROCE of 34% looks attractive. A 90 Cr market cap on just 9 Cr revenue with negative FCF is a speculative micro-cap bet, not a "cheap and good" business.
key_strengths: Stated ROCE 34.3% / ROE 24.8% — capital-light Shopify app niche
Zero debt; promoter holds 62.99%, FII 9.17% shows some institutional interest
Revenue grew 50% FY25 (6→9 Cr); EBIT margin expanded to ~67%
key_risks: Earnings yield only ~6.7% (EBIT 6/EV ~90) — fails Magic Formula cheapness test
Post-IPO equity ballooned 10→31 Cr; forward ROCE on enlarged capital base will be much lower than headline 34%
Micro-cap with tiny 9 Cr revenue and negative FCF (FY24 -4, FY25 -2) — speculative
red_flags: Reserves jumped from 3 to 21 Cr in FY25 — large fresh-capital raise distorts ROCE/ROE ratios
FCF negative two years running despite positive reported profit
P/E 18.6 rich for a 9 Cr-revenue micro-cap
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula perspective: I rank on earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and ROIC. EBIT of 6 Cr on EV of ~90 Cr gives ~6.7% yield — well below my 12% attractiveness bar. The headline 34% ROCE is flattering historical; post-IPO equity ballooned from 10 Cr to 31 Cr while EBIT is only 6 Cr, implying forward ROCE on deployed capital closer to ~19% once cash gets absorbed, and lower still if CWIP / investing outflows don't produce proportional EBIT growth. One metric is mediocre, the other is deteriorating — the textbook "avoid" quadrant.

Systematically, this fails my screen on size alone (90 Cr cap, 9 Cr revenue is too small for reliable rankings) and on valuation (P/E 18.6, EY 6.7%). The business may genuinely be a quality Shopify-ecosystem play with 63% promoter skin-in-the-game, but I don't pay 15x EBIT for a company whose return on freshly-raised capital is unproven. I'd need the price to roughly halve or EBIT to double before this appears on a Magic Formula list.
